name: Gareth Mensah

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government. Your answers are confidential. Tell me about a normal day at the accounting firm.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I get in before the phones start and check the shopkeepers' invoices against their bank entries. I lead the small accounts team, prepare returns and make the final judgment on odd entries; I like catching a missing receipt before it becomes a tax bill, but the owner's Friday pile of crumpled papers wears me down. I am 43, with a master's degree and a chartered accountancy qualification. I have never used an AI tool for our work; the familiar ledger and a conversation with the owner suit me. My partner Leila works evening care shifts, and we have two school-age children and a mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI mostly fizzles, the shop returns still arrive in boxes. A little automatic sorting might save half an hour, but someone must ask where the cash went.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team not to promise clients a new machine will clean their books. We can keep the same checking rota and answer the phone properly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Honestly, a quiet technology year would be welcome, but it would not fix our pay. My household has less than a month of expenses saved, the mortgage is due each month, and there are few accounting firms nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing the shop accounts and tax returns on our paid rota. From the next pay packet I would set aside forty in a separate cash account, if the mortgage and food are covered; I would keep the old paper check until the partner changes the procedure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious even in this mild picture because a late client payment can leave our account bare. I can manage the files, but a month of savings would be a luxury.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why start with forty?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: That is the amount left after the school lunches and mortgage in an ordinary month. If there is no surplus, I cannot honestly call it a saving.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you go to another firm for a rise?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would look at a posted senior vacancy, but there are few within reach of the children's school. I would not resign for a rumour of better pay.

say: I would keep our **checking rota** and answer shop owners directly.
I would avoid promising an **AI cure** for poor records.
think: My **low pay** still leaves little room after the mortgage.
Our **thin reserve** makes a late payment worrying even without major AI change.
do: Keep preparing **paid shop returns** under the existing checks.
Deposit **forty monthly** from pay only when food and mortgage are covered.
Check **posted local senior vacancies** for higher pay without resigning on rumours.
feel: I feel **anxious** about our small cash margin.
S0.quote: I can manage the files, but a month of savings would be a luxury.
fieldNote: His skill does not produce a **strong cushion**; routine bills already drive the worry in the mildest world.
His **real surplus** determines a deposit of forty; he does not count household cash twice.

steps.text: Keep paid shop returns and existing paper checks
Deposit forty from pay monthly only after mortgage and food
Check posted local senior vacancies for higher pay without resigning on rumours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Strong AI can read the same invoice patterns I teach new staff. It will reach our checking desk before any robot could reach a shop floor.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partners to show whose name remains on every return. I would also tell my team that a quick draft does not settle a disputed cash sale.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect a cut in junior checking hours, and my own lead hours could be trimmed if one person signs more files. I have excellent training, but our low wage and scant savings leave no slack if paid hours fall.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partner to let me check one month of AI-drafted returns against our signed originals on paid time. I would not use the tool on live client records without written approval; if my paid hours fall, I would apply only to posted senior accounts openings with written pay, hours and a start date that cover the mortgage, keeping existing paid shifts while available.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing hours, although I can still prove where a machine made a wrong assumption. My children cannot eat an impressive qualification.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the partner refuses the trial?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would continue our approved manual checks on the shifts still paid. I would not install a private tool on client files to make a point.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How far would you travel for a new post?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not so far that the fare eats the wage increase or my partner Leila must leave her evening care shifts for school pickup. A written offer must fit both pay and our pickup rota.

say: I would ask for a **named signer** on each return.
I would challenge the idea that **fast drafts** settle disputed sales.
think: My **lead hours** may shrink along with the junior checking rota.
Few local vacancies make a **pay cut** hard to reverse.
do: Compare **one month** of AI-drafted returns with signed originals on paid time only if approved; otherwise keep paid manual checks.
Seek a **posted senior opening** after hour cuts only with written mortgage-covering pay, hours, start date and workable pickup.
feel: I feel **anxious** about losing paid hours.
S1.quote: My children cannot eat an impressive qualification.
fieldNote: He resists a **live rollout** but would compare old signed files if the employer approves paid testing.
His alternative job needs written wages and a **school pickup** fit; a distant vacancy alone does not solve lost income.

steps.text: Compare month of AI drafts with signed originals only on approved paid time
After hour cuts seek posted senior job with written mortgage-covering pay hours start and pickup fit
Continue approved manual checks on offered paid shifts if partner refuses trial

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full AGI in 2028 could do the judgment on my tax files, not just sort invoices. Robots in 2031 are a later issue for physical work; our desk would already have changed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell staff that the firm must give proper notice if it ends paid posts. I would ask our accountancy body to press for clear severance terms, not a story about a robot three years away.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my senior post to go when the partners can buy the whole checking task cheaply. Leila's evening care wage will not pay our mortgage alone, and we have less than one month saved; I lie awake doing that sum.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would stop the planned weekend trip and put its monthly instalment into cash while wages arrive. I would ask the professional body to press the firm on severance; if my post ends in the first year after 2028, I would use the reserve and apply to actual posted payroll supervisor jobs, taking one only with written pay, hours and start date enough for the mortgage and school pickup. I would keep every paid shift offered before an actual ending, rather than resign on a forecast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect a large loss of our household wage and almost no runway. Being good at tax work does not make a new payroll vacancy appear.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why payroll if AGI can do calculations?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A payroll supervisor post is also desk work and could go next; I would treat a real paid opening as a bridge, not protection from AGI. I cannot make a safe new trade in two years without a paid place.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Leila's family help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Leila's mother could cover an occasional pickup, but she cannot replace a wage. I would ask only if an actual new shift clashes with the school run.

say: I would demand **notice and severance** before staff are cut.
I would say **2028 desk AGI** arrives before capable 2031 robots.
think: I expect my **senior accounting post** may end in 2028.
Leila's care wage cannot carry our **mortgage** without my pay.
do: Cancel **weekend trip** and save its monthly instalment while paid; use the existing reserve for bills after dismissal.
Ask the **professional body** to press for severance and keep offered paid shifts before any dismissal.
After job loss, take a **posted payroll supervisor role** only with written mortgage-covering pay, hours, start and pickup fit.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by expected wage loss.
S2.quote: Being good at tax work does not make a new payroll vacancy appear.
fieldNote: His **thin cash runway** and few local openings make the 2028 deadline materially different from a slow transition.
Payroll is still **thinking work**; he calls a posted paid role a temporary bridge, not a refuge from AGI.

steps.text: Cancel trip and deposit its monthly instalment while wages arrive
Ask accountancy body for severance while keeping offered paid shifts
After dismissal take posted payroll role only with written mortgage-covering pay hours start and pickup
Use reserve during search; ask partner’s mother for pickup only if new shift clashes

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years gives us time to see whether clients still pay for a human to explain a return. The screen judgment could still go in 2031, three years before capable robots reach hands-on jobs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partners to put a price on client meetings, not quietly add them to an unpaid lunch. I would say training only matters if there is paid work at its end.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I still think the tax checking wage is at risk, but I could prove demand for disputed-return meetings while I draw a salary. I cannot pay for a new course from our emergency cash.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask to lead one paid dispute meeting each quarter only if the partner assigns it within my hours. If that work brings a written client adviser vacancy before or after 2031, I would move only with signed pay, hours and a start date covering our mortgage and pickup; otherwise I would keep the paid accounts work available and use free professional notes to prepare. In the first year after AGI, if those accounts hours disappear, I would use the same vacancy rule while holding any remaining paid shifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious; five years gives me a test, not a guaranteed salary. The thin savings still make a missed month frightening.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you study for another qualification?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if the firm pays the fee and gives paid study hours for a defined client role. Otherwise the free case notes will do while I still have a paid job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What counts as demand?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A billed meeting that the partner assigns and a client attends, not a pleasant chat by the door. I want the job number in writing before I call it a path.

say: I would ask the firm to **bill client meetings** rather than expect unpaid favours.
I would make any **course fee** depend on paid work and study time.
think: The **tax checking wage** remains exposed in 2031.
A **billed dispute meeting** could test whether a human adviser role pays.
do: Lead **quarterly paid disputes** only when the partner assigns them within paid hours.
Study **free case notes** while paid; take a course only with funded fees and paid hours for a defined role.
Before or after 2031, take a **posted client adviser role** only with signed mortgage-covering pay, hours, start and pickup fit.
feel: I feel **anxious** because a client role may never pay.
S3.quote: I want the job number in writing before I call it a path.
fieldNote: He tests **billed demand** on his paid schedule, rejecting unpaid client chats as evidence of income.
His paid-work fallback and **free notes** matter because the household cannot self-fund a speculative qualification.

steps.text: Keep paid accounts shifts and lead assigned paid quarterly disputes
Use free notes; take defined-role course only with funded fee and paid hours
Take posted adviser job before or after 2031 with signed mortgage-covering pay hours start pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A decade lets my children finish school before the accounting desk faces AGI in 2036. Robots in 2039 do not extend the life of tax checking, but ten years changes our mortgage arithmetic.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the partners to give staff dates for any planned change instead of vague promises. I would tell colleagues I want a paid client role, not a ceremonial new title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think our returns may still be automated, yet I could bring the loan balance down before 2036. I would rather keep steady paid work than gamble on a distant firm we know nothing about.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From each wage I would pay an extra thirty toward mortgage principal only if the lender confirms no penalty and the month's essentials are covered. I would ask for a paid senior client role when a written vacancy exists; in the first year after 2036, if my return work ends, I would take that or another posted role only with signed wage, hours and start date that fit the remaining mortgage and school travel. Until work actually ends, I would retain the paid returns and not resign for a verbal promise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the eventual desk change, but I can plan the loan without pretending I can retrain for free. The worry about this month's bills remains.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you retire early?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, we cannot live on less than a month's savings. I expect to work through the children's later schooling.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the lender charges a fee?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would keep the thirty as cash instead of making an extra loan payment, provided food and the regular mortgage are paid. A mortgage prepayment fee would erase the small advantage of paying thirty extra.

say: I would seek **dated plans** from the partners.
I would insist a **client title** comes with paid work.
think: I expect **return checking** may vanish by 2036.
Ten years lets me reduce the **mortgage balance** while earnings continue.
do: Allocate **thirty monthly** only after essentials: pay principal if penalty-free, otherwise retain cash.
Keep **paid return work** until it ends or a real offer starts.
Take a **posted client role** only with signed mortgage-covering pay, hours, start date and school-travel fit.
feel: I feel **anxious** about the distant desk change and this month's bills.
S4.quote: A mortgage prepayment fee would erase the small advantage of paying thirty extra.
fieldNote: The decade improves his **loan plan** but does not turn his present thin reserve into security.
He refuses early retirement and insists on a **paid vacancy** before leaving available return work.

steps.text: Set aside thirty monthly only after essentials; pay principal if penalty-free, otherwise save cash
Keep paid return work while offered until written job starts
Take posted client job only with signed mortgage-covering pay hours start and school fit

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because our wage could go before we have a cushion. A written notice period, severance and a real paid vacancy with mortgage-covering terms would help more than a lecture about being flexible.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask how long a family can live on a senior title when its salary is low. My chartered qualification is real, but our cupboard does not hold a month's pay.

headlineQuote: My chartered qualification is real, but our cupboard does not hold a month's pay.
portrait: Gareth is a **43-year-old senior accountant** who leads shop accounts and has a master's and chartered qualification.
His **low pay**, mortgage and less than one month saved leave little room despite high skill.
He **never uses AI** and requires paid, approved tests before touching live client files.
He would test billed client work over time, but a **written paid vacancy** governs any move.
His **partner Leila** works evening care shifts, and their two school-age children depend on both wages.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** world threatens his wage before his family builds a cash runway.
whatWouldHelp: He wants **notice and severance**, plus a posted role with written mortgage-covering pay.
